cues.zh: Rust 尤其就是为满足这类极高性能需求而设计的。它是一门系统编程语言，面向那些

cues.en: the the big problem with async IO is that
cues.zh: 异步 I/O 最大的问题是

cues.zh: 它的工作方式是：当你调用 I/O，也就是系统调用时，它会立即返回，然后最终你可以继续做其他工作。但你的程序要负责弄清楚如何，

cues.zh: 比起编写使用阻塞式 I/O 的程序。因此，很多想面向这类可扩展网络服务的语言

cues.en: have been trying to come up with solutions for this problem that, like, take it, make it not the end user's problem but a part of the language or part of the libraries.
cues.zh: 一直在尝试为这个问题想出解决方案，比如把它承担下来，让它不再是终端用户的问题，而是语言或库的一部分。

cues.en: And so the first solution that Rust
cues.zh: 所以 Rust 最初的解决方案

cues.en: started with was this idea of green threads, which have been successful in a lot of languages.
cues.zh: 是绿色线程这个思路，它在很多语言里都取得了成功。

cues.en: And so
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: green threads basically look like blocking IO. They look like spawning threads
cues.zh: 绿色线程基本上看起来就像阻塞式 IO。看起来就像启动线程

cues.en: and then just blocking on IO. And everything looks exactly the same as if you were using the native OS primitives,
cues.zh: 然后只是在 IO 上阻塞。一切都和你使用原生操作系统原语时一模一样，

cues.en: but they've been designed as part of the language runtime
cues.zh: 但它们被设计为语言运行时的一部分

cues.en: to
cues.zh: 以便

cues.en: be optimized for this use case of having these network services,
cues.zh: 针对这种网络服务的场景做优化，

cues.en: which are trying to responding, you know, thousands, tens of thousands, maybe millions of
cues.zh: 也就是要同时响应成千、上万，甚至可能上百万个

cues.en: green threads at the same time.

cues.en: A language, I think, right now that is, like, having a lot of success with this model is Go, where they're called Go routines. And so it's very normal for a Go program to have tens of thousands of these running at the same time because
cues.zh: 我觉得目前在这种模型上非常成功的一门语言是 Go，它们在那里叫 goroutine。所以一个 Go 程序同时运行几万个 goroutine 非常正常，因为

cues.en: they're very cheap to spawn, unlike OS threads.
cues.zh: 与 OS 线程不同，它们的创建成本非常低。

cues.en: And so just the advantage of green threads is that the
cues.zh: 所以绿色线程的优势就在于

cues.en: memory overhead
cues.zh: 内存开销

cues.en: when you spawn an OS thread is much higher because you create this huge stack for for each OS thread. Whereas green threads, the way they normally work is that you'll spawn a thread that starts with a very small stack that can grow over time. And so spawning a bunch of new threads that aren't using a lot of memory yet is, you know, much cheaper.
cues.zh: 创建 OS 线程时内存开销要高得多，因为每个 OS 线程都要创建一个巨大的栈。而绿色线程通常的工作方式是，创建的线程一开始只有很小的栈，之后可以增长。所以创建一堆还没用多少内存的新线程，你知道，要便宜得多。

cues.en: And, also, a problem with using, like, the operating system primitives is that you depend on the operating system for scheduling,
cues.zh: 另外，使用操作系统原语还有个问题：你得依赖操作系统来做调度，

cues.en: which means that you have to switch
cues.zh: 这意味着你必须切换

cues.en: from your program's memory space into the kernel space, and the context switching
cues.zh: 从程序的内存空间进入内核空间，而上下文切换

cues.zh: 会带来大量开销，如果你……一旦你开始有，你知道，数万个线程都在被，比如，

cues.en: switched between really quickly.
cues.zh: 非常快速地来回切换。

cues.en: And so by keeping that scheduling in the same program, you avoid these context switches and that reduces the overhead.
cues.zh: 所以，把调度保留在同一个程序里，就能避免这些上下文切换，从而降低开销。

cues.en: And so green threading is a pretty good model that works for a lot of languages,

cues.zh: 都使用这个模型。

cues.zh: 具体来说，是因为

cues.zh: 我谈到的第一个问题，也就是

cues.en: it was imposing costs on people who didn't need it. So if you just wanted to write a Rust program that didn't need to use green threads, that wasn't a network service, you still had to have this language runtime that was responsible for scheduling all of your green threads.
cues.zh: 它把成本强加给了不需要它的人。所以，如果你只是想写一个不需要使用绿色线程的 Rust 程序，一个不是网络服务的程序，你仍然得有一个语言运行时，负责调度你所有的绿色线程。

cues.zh: 所以，

cues.zh: 我们见过很多人成功采用 Rust 的路径之一，就是他们有个大的 C 程序，想开始用 Rust。于是他们开始把一点点 Rust 集成进他们的程……集成进他们的程序里。就是让代码中的某一段用 Rust 来跑。

cues.zh: 但

cues.zh: 问题在于，如果你必须先搭好这个运行时才能调用 Rust，那……只让程序的一小部分用 Rust 就太不划算了，因为调用 Rust 函数之前你得先把运行时搭起来。

And so it makes it very easy to call between Rust and c, and it's very cheap, which is one of the key things that makes Rust really successful.
cues.zh: 所以，在 1.0 前不久，我们从语言中移除了绿色线程。我们去掉了这个语言运行时，现在，你知道，我们的运行时基本上和 C 一样。这使得 Rust 和 C 之间互相调用非常容易，而且开销很低，这也是 Rust 如此成功的关键原因之一。

cues.zh: 但我们意识到，它需要是基于库的解决方案。我们需要某种方式，

cues.en: providing
cues.zh: 提供

cues.en: a value that you may not have evaluated yet. And so you can manipulate it before

cues.en: which was that, you know, when using features, the error messages are inscrutable.
cues.zh: 说的是，你知道，使用 feature 时，错误信息晦涩难懂。

cues.en: Having to use ref cell or clone everything for each feature leads to overcompanied code and it makes me wish that Rust just had garbage collection,
cues.zh: 每用一个 feature 都得用 RefCell，或者把东西全都 clone 一遍，这会导致代码过度复杂，让我真希望 Rust 干脆有垃圾回收，

cues.en: which is, yeah, not great feedback.
cues.zh: 这反馈嘛，确实不怎么样。

cues.en: So looking at the situation maybe a year, year and a half ago,
cues.zh: 所以，看看大概一年、一年半前的情况，

cues.en: it was clear that there were sort of two problems that needed to be to make, that needed to be solved in order to make features
cues.zh: 很明显，有两个问题需要解决，才能让功能

cues.en: more usable for people. And the first was we needed better error messages, and so the easiest way to do that is to build the syntax into the language and then they can hook into all of our diagnostics and error message
cues.zh: 对人们更易用。第一个是我们需要更好的错误信息，而最简单的方法是把语法内建到语言里，这样它们就能接入我们所有的诊断信息和错误信息

cues.en: support so that you can have really good error messages for async await.
cues.zh: 支持，从而为 async await 提供真正好用的错误信息。

cues.en: But the second was that most of these errors people were running into were actually
cues.zh: 但第二点是，人们遇到的这些错误，实际上大多

cues.en: then bouncing off a sort of obscure problem, which is called the borrowing problem,
cues.zh: 都撞上了一个有点晦涩的问题，叫做借用问题，

cues.en: where
cues.zh: 也就是

cues.en: there was this fundamental limitations in the way the features were designed that made it to something... Really common pattern was not possible to express.
cues.zh: 这些特性的设计方式存在根本性限制，导致某种……非常常见的模式无法表达。

cues.en: And that problem was that you can't,
cues.zh: 而问题就在于，你没法，

cues.en: in the original design of features, you could not borrow
cues.zh: 在最初的功能设计中，你不能借用

cues.en: across an await point. So if you were to await something, you couldn't have any references that were alive at that time. And so when people were having these problems that they were bouncing off of, what they were actually, ultimately what they were doing was they were trying to borrow while
cues.zh: 跨 await 点。所以如果你要 await 某个东西，那时就不能有任何仍然存活的引用。于是当人们遇到这些让他们卡住的问题时，他们实际上、最终在做的是，他们想一边借用，而

cues.en: they were awaiting, and they couldn't do that.
cues.zh: 一边 await，却做不到。

cues.en: And so if we could just make it so that was allowed, then most of these errors would go away and everything would be much easier to use, and you could just kind of write normal Rust code with async and await, and it would all work.
cues.zh: 所以，只要我们能允许这种情况，大多数这类错误就会消失，一切都会好用得多，你就能正常写带 async 和 await 的 Rust 代码，而且都能正常工作。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: these kinds of borrows during awaits are extremely common because just the natural API service of Rust is to have references in the API.
cues.zh: 这类在 await 期间的借用极其常见，因为 Rust 的 API 天生就会带引用。

cues.en: And so,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: but the problem with futures is that
cues.zh: 但 future 的问题在于，

cues.en: when you actually compile the future, which has to restore all that state,
cues.zh: 当你真正编译 future 时，它必须恢复所有这些状态，

cues.en: when you have some references to something else that's in the same stack frame, what you end up getting is this sort of self referential future.
cues.zh: 当你有指向同一栈帧中其他内容的引用时，最终得到的就是这种自引用 future。

cues.en: And so here's some code from the original, like, get user method
cues.zh: 这是原始代码里的一段，比如 get user 方法

cues.en: where we have this SQL string and then when we call query with it,
cues.zh: 这里有个 SQL 字符串，然后我们调用 query 时把它传进去，

cues.en: we use pass a reference to the SQL string.
cues.zh: 我们传的是这个 SQL 字符串的引用。

cues.en: And so the problem here is that
cues.zh: 这里的问题在于

cues.en: this
cues.zh: 这个

cues.en: reference to the SQL string is a reference to something else that's being stored in the same future state.
cues.zh: 对 SQL 字符串的引用，指向的是存在同一个 future 状态里的另一个东西。

cues.en: And so it becomes this sort of self referential struct where you have these are the fields of the future in theory if it were, you a real struct.
cues.zh: 于是它就成了这种自引用结构体，理论上如果 future 真的是个结构体，这些就是它的字段。

cues.en: It would have, you know, the database handle that you were in the self
cues.zh: 它里面会有，你知道，那个数据库句柄，就是你在 self 的

cues.en: aspect of it. Then it would also have the SQL string
cues.zh: 那部分里放的那个。然后它还会有 SQL 字符串

cues.en: and the reference to the SQL string, which is ultimately a reference pointing back to a field of the same struct.
cues.zh: 以及对 SQL 字符串的引用，而它最终指回同一个结构体里的某个字段。

cues.en: And self referential structs are sort of a really hard problem that we don't have a general solution for.
cues.zh: 自引用结构体是个相当棘手的问题，我们没有通用解法。

cues.en: And the reason that we can't allow you to have reference to the same structs is that when
cues.zh: 我们不能允许你持有指向同一结构体的引用，原因是当

cues.en: you move that struct,
cues.zh: 你移动那个结构体时，

cues.en: then what happens is that we make a new copy of the struct in the location that you're moving it to, and the old copy becomes invalidated.
cues.zh: 实际发生的是，我们在你移动到的位置新建一份结构体副本，而旧的那份就失效了。

cues.en: But when you make that copy, the reference that was self referential is still pointing
cues.zh: 但当你做这个复制时，那个自引用的引用仍然指向

cues.en: to the old copy,
cues.zh: 旧的副本，

cues.en: and that
cues.zh: 这就会

cues.en: becomes a dangling pointer, and it's the kind of memory issues that Rust has to prevent.
cues.zh: 变成悬垂指针，而这正是 Rust 必须防止的一类内存问题。

cues.en: So we can't have self referential structs because if you move them around, then they become invalidated.
cues.zh: 所以不能有自引用结构体，因为一旦移动它们，它们就会失效。

cues.en: But what made this, like, really frustrating in the futures case was that
cues.zh: 但在 Future 的场景里，真正让人沮丧的是

cues.en: we actually don't really need to move these futures around.
cues.zh: 我们其实并不需要来回移动这些 Future。

cues.en: So if you remember the model where the future is in the heap and a handle to it is getting passed back and forth between the reactor and the executor,
cues.zh: 所以如果你还记得那个模型：future 放在堆上，指向它的句柄在 reactor 和 executor 之间来回传递，

cues.en: the future itself never actually moves. And so it's totally fine for the future to contain self references as long as you never move it and you don't need to move it. So what we really needed to solve this problem was some way to express in the API of futures that while you're pulling it, you're not allowed to move it around. And then if we just could express that somehow,
cues.zh: future 本身其实从不移动。因此，只要永远不移动它、也不需要移动它，future 包含自引用就完全没问题。所以我们真正需要解决这个问题的方法是，在 future 的 API 中以某种方式表达：当你拉取它时，不允许把它移来移去。然后如果我们能设法表达这一点，

cues.en: then we
cues.zh: 那我们

cues.en: could allow
cues.zh: 就能允许

cues.en: these kinds of self references in the body of the future, and then we could just have these references
cues.zh: 在 future 的主体中允许这类自引用，然后我们就能直接拥有这些引用

cues.en: in your async functions and everything would work.
cues.zh: 在你的 async 函数中，一切就能正常工作。

cues.en: And so we were working on this problem and ultimately
cues.zh: 于是我们一直在研究这个问题，最终

cues.en: we came out with this
cues.zh: 我们提出了这个

cues.en: new API called pin.
cues.zh: 名为 pin 的新 API。

cues.en: And so pin is a sort of adapter around other pointer types where they become this pinned reference instead of just a normal reference. And a pinned reference, in addition to whatever other guarantees it has, it guarantees that
cues.zh: 所以 pin 算是其他指针类型的一种适配器，让它们变成这种 pinned 引用，而不只是普通引用。而 pinned 引用除了它本身拥有的其他保证之外，还保证

cues.en: the reference will
cues.zh: 该引用将

cues.en: never... The value that the reference is pointing to will never be moved again. And so guarantees that it's going to stay in the same place until eventually it gets deallocated.
cues.zh: 永远不会……该引用所指向的值将永远不会再次移动。并且因此保证它会一直待在同一个位置，直到最终被释放。

cues.en: And so if you have something in your API which says that it has to be taken by PIN, then you know that it will never be moved again and you can have these kinds of self referential structs.
cues.zh: 所以，如果你的 API 里有东西规定必须用 PIN 接收，那你就知道它再也不会被移动，于是就能有这种自引用结构体。

cues.en: And so we changed the way the features work so that now instead of just being a boxed feature, it's a boxed feature behind a pin. So we know that wherever we boxed it up, put it in the heap, it's guaranteed now by part of the pin API
cues.zh: 所以我们改了 feature 的工作方式：现在它不再只是一个装箱的 feature，而是 PIN 后面的装箱 feature。于是我们知道，不管我们在哪里把它装箱、放到堆上，现在都由 PIN API 的一部分保证

cues.en: that it will never move again.
cues.zh: 它再也不会移动。

cues.en: And then, you know, when you pull the feature, instead of just passing a normal reference to it, we pass the pinned reference to it. And so the feature knows that it can't be moved.
cues.zh: 然后，当你拉取这个 future 时，不是传给它一个普通引用，而是传给它一个 pinned 引用。这样 future 就知道自己不能被移动了。

cues.en: And the trick here that makes this all work is that you can only get an unpinned reference out of a pinned reference in unsafe code. It's an unsafe function to be able to do that.
cues.zh: 让这一切成立的关键在于：只有在 unsafe 代码里，才能从 pinned 引用中取出未 pin 的引用。能做到这一点的是一个 unsafe 函数。

cues.en: And so the API
cues.zh: 所以这个 API

cues.zh: 大致长这样：

cues.en: you have pinned, which is just a wrapper around
cues.zh: 你有一个 Pin，它只是对

cues.en: a pointer type. It doesn't have any runtime overhead or anything. It just demarcates it as being pinned.
cues.zh: 指针类型的一层包装。它没有任何运行时开销之类的东西，只是标记出它被 pin 住了。

cues.en: And then
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: a pinned box can be converted into a pinned reference. But the only way to convert a pinned reference into an unpinned reference is to use an unsafe function.
cues.zh: pinned Box 可以转换成 pinned 引用。但把 pinned 引用转换成非 pinned 引用的唯一方法，是使用 unsafe 函数。

cues.zh: 所以

cues.zh: 我们随后做的就是，直接改了 features API，让它
